newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.5 percent in July.
newsitem.headline: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.5 percent in July.

text.p: Canada's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, rose 0.5 percent in July after staying unchanged in June, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast real GDP to rise 0.45 percent in July.
Note: GDP figures are in billions of dollars, seasonally adjusted at annual rates at factor cost, constant 1986 dollars.
Statistics Canada said a surge in manufacturing production helped boost GDP in July and economic activity improved in most sectors.
"A second consecutive increase in retail trade, further gains in wholesale trade and construction, and a rebound in transportation and storage services were particularly notable," the agency said.
Manufacturing production grew by 1.8 percent in July, exceeding the December 1994 peak by 0.8 percent.
The finance and mining groups, communication services and utilities also posted modest gains, Statistics Canada said.
Activity in community and personal services remained little changed in July and economic activity in forestry continued to decline, Statistics Canada said.
(For more information from Statistics Canada contact Michel Girard, Industry Measures and Analysis Division, at 613-951-9145).
